things_a_buyer_should_know: The whole quote is one email line. All prices are per kg, but the RFx asks for per-piece prices (and per set for PT-501/502). Converting needs the RFx estimated weights, and the vendor has not confirmed them.
The 3-ply rate is written as just '38', with no currency or unit. It is read as INR/kg because it follows '₹42/kg'. Confirm this with the vendor.

The scope of the '3-ply' rate is unclear. It clearly covers the 3-ply RSC cartons CB-101 to CB-110. I also applied it, at medium confidence, to the 3-ply die-cut trays (DT), partition sets (PT) and layer pads (LP). The vendor may have meant those as 'rest same as last year'. Printing, die-cutting and conversion costs are not addressed.

The 7-ply lines (CB-301 to CB-303) and the 2-ply roll (CR-701) have no price. They fall under 'rest same as last year', and the old contract price must be looked up. The 7-ply is not covered by the 5-ply rate.
Freight is extra, but the RFx asked for a delivered (FOR Manesar) price. The freight cost is not quantified, so the quote cannot be compared directly with delivered quotes.

The vendor gave no validity, GST treatment, lead time, payment terms, MOQ or price-variation clause. It also did not answer any of the questionnaire (Q1 to Q7) and attached no certificates (ISO 9001, COA, food-safety declaration).
Sonipat appears only in the email signature. It is not explicitly stated as the supplying plant location.
The rates are quoted as firm 'per kg'. Billing on actual weight could differ from the RFx estimated weights, which would make the per-piece cost uncertain.
